narration.text: Why one star flees at 1,755 km/s.
That's almost 0.6% of the speed of light.
S5-HVS1 was flung out by our galaxy's central black hole.
It may have been half of a binary pair.
One star was captured, and its partner was launched.
It's now about 29,000 light-years from Earth.
It will never return to the Milky Way.
So black holes don't just swallow stars. They throw them.
